Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: In the darkness beneath the river, an old tie sinks slowly through the water.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: A shaft of light from somewhere above breaks through the surface, catching the tie's faded diagonal stripes.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Then the current begins to reverse. The water draws back the way it came. The soaked fabric slowly dries, and the silt clinging to it vanishes in turn.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: By the time the sound of running water has faded completely, a clock begins to tick somewhere in the distance.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Once.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Then again.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The Old House on the Hill — Living Room.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Heavy clouds hang beyond the windows. The rain has yet to fall.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: 8:41 AM. Nineteen minutes until they are supposed to leave.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man is crouched by the entryway, going through the girl's backpack. His canvas sneakers are waiting by the door, their laces loosely tied.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The girl already has her coat on. She sits on the shoe cabinet with the amusement park map hugged to her chest, one toe tapping steadily against the cabinet door.

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: Dad, how much longer? If we don't leave now, we'll miss the first ride on the Ferris wheel!

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Then maybe don't pack half the house. Hmmm... binoculars... and a broken flashlight? What do you need all this for?

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: I fixed it ages ago! And we need the binoculars to find our house. We made a deal yesterday, remember? When the Ferris wheel gets all the way to the top, first one to spot our roof wins.

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: And this time, no keeping your eyes shut the whole way just because you're scared!

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man tries the flashlight, looking less than convinced. The bulb flickers twice, then dies.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Before he can say a word, the girl snatches it back, clutching it to her chest along with the map. A white Ferris wheel car has been circled in red on the page.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The phone on the table starts to buzz.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: He lets the first call go unanswered. When the same name lights up the screen again, the man glances at the girl, then picks up the phone.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Hello... This morning? But I already took the day off. Bruce is still in the hospital? But the proposal...

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: All right. Got it. I'll be there in half an hour.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: When the call ends, the man keeps the darkened phone in his hand and says nothing for a long moment.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The girl falls quiet too. She lowers her head and slowly folds the map along its old creases.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Something came up at work. The guy covering for me is still in the hospital. I promise I'll be back before noon. We can go this afternoon instead, okay?

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: But the forecast says it's going to pour at noon. They shut down the Ferris wheel when the weather gets bad. You were the one who told me that. Did you forget?

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Then... next Sunday? This time we'll leave at eight-thirty. I—

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: You said that last Sunday too.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man looks out the window. The rain has yet to fall, but so little daylight remains that the glass can barely hold a reflection.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Every excuse he had ready rises to his lips. One by one, he swallows them back.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The girl folds the map again. The car circled in red disappears into the fold.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: ...I'm sorry. I really am. This one's my fault. When I get back, I'll find a way to make it up to you, okay?

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: For now, I need to find that stupid tie.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The Old House on the Hill — Bedroom.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The half-open wardrobe cuts off part of the dim daylight coming through the window.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The gray sweater has been laid back on the bed. The man changes into a white shirt and digs the rarely worn tie out from the bottom of the wardrobe.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Its style is a little dated, and a stubborn crease runs across the fabric from having been folded away for so long.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: He tries twice, but the knot still hangs loose and shapeless. The girl watches from the doorway for a long while. At last, she walks over and takes both ends of the tie from him.

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: The wide end goes on top. Then around the back. Mom's shown you this a million times.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: She has. I'm just terrible at remembering it.

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: You never forget anything for work.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man opens his mouth to defend himself. But every answer he can think of only makes the girl sound more right.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man bends down and lets her tie it for him. Her hands are still small, halfway through, she loops the fabric the wrong way and has to pull it apart and start again.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: When she finally slides the knot up to his throat, she tugs a little too hard and makes him cough.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: A joke rises to his lips. Then he sees the girl's mouth drawn into a tight line and swallows it back.

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: It's still crooked. Don't move. I'll tie it again.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: There's no time. No one else will be able to tell.

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: I can.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: It's fine. Just leave it. Every time I see, it'll remind me I still owe you a ride on Ferris wheel.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The Old House on the Hill — Entryway.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The rain has begun.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man slips on his dress shoes and picks up his briefcase. Then he reaches over and straightens the strap of the girl's backpack where it has folded over.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Mom should be back from the grocery store in town soon. Go upstairs and wait for her, all right?

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: The rain's getting worse, so don't go outside by yourself. Promise me.

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: ...I know.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: I'll try to be back by noon. Wait for me.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man turns and walks out into the rain. Just as the door is about to close, the narrow end of his tie slips free from behind the knot.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The knot was crooked to begin with. Now it sits a little farther off-center.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The girl sees it. She almost calls him back. But she is still angry.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: While she hesitates, the door swings shut. As the gap narrows to nothing, her parted lips close with it.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: At exactly nine, the minute hand reaches the final mark on the clock face.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: By the door, only the sneakers that were meant to leave with him are still waiting.

Speaker: SpecialNarration
Dialogue: IT WASN'T YOUR FAULT

Speaker: SpecialNarration
Dialogue: YOU DON'T BELONG HERE
